post.caption: Lady Liberty's torch joined a parade. The statue's first torch stayed up from 1886 until 1984. In 1916, the flame was rebuilt with colored glass. The glass leaked, and water damaged the torch for decades. In 1984, it was judged too damaged to repair. Then it traveled to Pasadena and joined the Rose Parade. A new torch, copied from the original design, went up in 1985. The new flame is covered in 24 karat gold. The old torch is now kept in the Statue of Liberty Museum. It is 16 feet tall and weighs 3,600 pounds.
